gap: No result ChatGPT got states how much AC energy each station actually delivered when reviewers measured it. Every page applies a flat 85% to the rated Wh, and that hides the fact that the BLUETTI Elite 300 measured 2,670 Wh: short of the roughly 2,800 Wh an 8-hour night on a 350 W EverFlo needs, so it gives about 7.6 h rather than covering the night.
standout_why: I compared against the cited blackoutwise.com/will-it-run/home-oxygen-concentrator-5l, the cited willitrunpower.com/best-power-station-for/oxygen-concentrator, our own page and the ChatGPT answers. All of them work out hours as rated Wh × 0.85 ÷ watts. Willrun adds a 15 W inverter draw, and 40 W for the F3800. None gives a measured AC output for any station. None says that the Elite 300's 4,800 W 'surge' is BLUETTI's Power Lifting figure, which is for resistive loads only, so it says nothing about starting a compressor. Willrun lists the Elite 300's 10 ms switchover as a maker claim; nobody gives StorageReview's measured 8 ms. The rivals already cover concentrator watts by model and flow, so that part isn't new.
decides: It confirms the pick structure and corrects one implied promise. Measured AC output runs from 85% of rated (DELTA 3, Jackery 1000 v2) to 92% (Elite 200 V2), so the flat 85% rule is fair to slightly pessimistic. At 350 W, though, even the largest station on our page, the Elite 300 at 2,670 Wh measured, falls about 25 minutes short of 8 hours. For overnight cover the shopper needs an expandable unit plus a battery: AC200L + B300K, or DELTA 3 + extra batteries. The 1 kWh units (DELTA 3, C1000 Gen 2, Jackery 1000 v2) land within 0.1 h of each other, about 2.5 to 2.6 h, so capacity doesn't separate them; switchover and price have to.

findings.label: Measured usable AC energy, full discharge
findings.source_title: BLUETTI Elite 300 review: 3,014Wh, 2,400W and an 8ms UPS switchover in a 58-pound box (StorageReview, Dylan Bryan, 2026-08-27)
findings.note: Dylan Bryan at StorageReview measured 2.67 kWh out before depletion and 3.49 kWh in from the wall for a 0–100% charge. Out ÷ rated = 2,670 ÷ 3,014.4 = 88.6%. At 350 W (EverFlo average): 2,670 ÷ 350 = 7.6 h. An 8-hour night at 350 W needs 2,800 Wh, so it is about 130 Wh, roughly 22 minutes, short. The review doesn't state the discharge load.

findings.label: Measured UPS switchover, grid to battery
findings.note: Measured with a Quarch power analyzer while watching the AC waveforms as line power was removed. BLUETTI claims 10 ms. StorageReview paraphrases the manual as saying the UPS feature 'is not intended for data servers or workstations that require a high-performance UPS', and BLUETTI disclaims liability for that use. This was not a test with a concentrator.

findings.label: Continuous vs 'surge' normalised
findings.value: 2,400 W continuous; the 4,800 W figure is Power Lifting for resistive loads only, and output stays at 2,400 W in that mode
findings.note: So 4,800 W is not a compressor-start surge rating. Even so, 2,400 W continuous is about 6.9× a 350 W concentrator.

findings.label: Measured usable AC energy, full discharge
findings.source_title: Portable power meets lab-grade reliability: BLUETTI Elite 200 V2 review (StorageReview, Dylan Dougherty, 2025-04-25)
findings.note: Recharging took 2.44 kWh. 1,910 ÷ 2,073.6 = 92.1%. At 350 W: 1,910 ÷ 350 = 5.5 h. The discharge load isn't stated; the separate UPS test drew 986 W to 1.1 kW. The 15 ms switchover is BLUETTI's claim and was not measured.

findings.label: Measured usable AC energy
findings.note: Taken from the 'Measured Energy Output' line in OutdoorGearLab's spec table. The test load isn't stated. At 350 W: 870 ÷ 350 = 2.5 h.

findings.label: Measured usable AC energy
findings.source_title: Anker SOLIX C1000 Gen 2 review (OutdoorGearLab, Kenji Mowrey, 2026-07-23)
findings.note: Measured with a light-bar load bank of unstated wattage. The page contradicts itself: the text says 890 of 1,024 Wh = 87%, while the spec table gives 1,056 Wh claimed and 80% usable. I used the text, since 1,024 Wh matches Anker's page. At 350 W: 890 ÷ 350 = 2.5 h.

findings.label: Maker specs as stated
findings.value: 1,024 Wh; 2,000 W continuous, 3,000 W peak; UPS 10 ms ('under 10 ms' in the feature list)
findings.source_title: Anker SOLIX C1000 Gen 2 product page, Anker SOLIX US
findings.note: No footnote on the page limits the UPS for medical or life-support devices. The page lists 'Medical Devices' as a use. It showed no price.

findings.label: Measured usable AC energy
findings.source_title: Jackery Explorer 1000 v2 review (OutdoorGearLab, Kenji Mowrey, 2026-07-23)
findings.note: The load isn't given beyond running 'near its max wattage'. At 350 W: 910 ÷ 350 = 2.6 h.

findings.label: Maker's own runtime inputs (BLUETTI formula quoted by Notebookcheck)
findings.value: DoD 95%, efficiency 93%, self-consumption 12 W; about 5.0 h at 350 W
findings.source_title: Bluetti AC200L hands-on review (Notebookcheck, Polly Allcock, 2024-08-05, updated 2026-02-18)
findings.note: BLUETTI's formula: hours = Wh × DoD × η ÷ (load + self-consumption) = 2,048 × 0.95 × 0.93 ÷ (350 + 12) = 1,809 ÷ 362 = 5.0 h. That equals 88% of rated, net of the 12 W idle. This is the maker's model, not a measurement; Notebookcheck published no measured Wh.

unsourced: BLUETTI AC200L measured usable AC Wh: nextPit's review URL now redirects to inside-digital.de, so I couldn't open the reported 1.68 kWh figure, and Notebookcheck's review has no measurement.
Measured UPS switchover for EcoFlow DELTA 3, Anker SOLIX C1000 Gen 2, Jackery Explorer 1000 v2, BLUETTI AC200L and Elite 200 V2: I found maker claims only.

Each maker's own manual wording on using the UPS with medical or life-support devices: the BLUETTI Elite 300 manual PDF is over 10 MB and too large to fetch, downloading it needed shell approval, and the EcoFlow DELTA 3 manual on manuals.plus returned 403.
Discharge load in OutdoorGearLab's and StorageReview's capacity tests: neither states the wattage, so the measured percentages are not shown to apply at a 350 W concentrator load.
Prices for every candidate: I spent the tool budget on measured capacity, Anker's C1000 Gen 2 page showed no price, and the BLUETTI Elite 300 product page failed with a redirect loop.
